name: DAPT
seoDesc: DAPT: answer 10 values and the page computes the result when you press Calculate — formula and worked example included.
summary: The DAPT calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 9 fields it asks for and it works out DAPT score straight away, with the formula shown underneath. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the DAPT calculator work?
sections.html:
The DAPT calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports DAPT score in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the age).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
What you supply, field by field
FieldUnits and meaning
Agepick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as <65 years, 65-74 years and ≥75 years. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
Diabetesa single on/off switch — tick it for “Presence of diabetes mellitus”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Prior MIa single on/off switch — tick it for “Prior myocardial infarction or percutaneous coronary intervention”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
MIa single on/off switch — tick it for “Myocardial infarction at presentation”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Stenta single on/off switch — tick it for “Stent diameter less than 3 mm”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Veina single on/off switch — tick it for “Vein graft stent”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
CHF hisotrya single on/off switch — tick it for “History of congestive heart failure or LVEF <30%”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Smokinga single on/off switch — tick it for “Current or past smoker”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
PE stenta single on/off switch — tick it for “Paclitaxel-Eluting stent”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.

9 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the DAPT calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

DAPT score=(CHF hisotry + MI + PE stent + age + diabetes + prior MI + smoking + stent + vein)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The DAPT calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the DAPT calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 9 drop-downs on this page offer a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

sections.title: How do you check the answer yourself?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time — age for instance — and watch which results move. A result that stays put does not depend on it.
  • Try a round value you can work out in your head. If the answer matches your mental arithmetic, the inputs are on the scale you assumed.
  • Re-enter the same figure and confirm the result is stable; a number that moves when you press Calculate again is a sign that a field is still empty.

faq.q: What does the DAPT calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns DAPT score. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the DAPT calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 9 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (9 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports DAPT score = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the DAPT calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
